does_not_apply_when: small pilots where the founder is deliberately the face of the brand

signal.check: The store is planning to scale content volume past what the founder alone can film.

expected_effect.size: unknown; craft claim, no lift given

risk.note: A format-selection decision only.

steps: List candidate formats and rate each on whether a team could film 15 in a day without the founder.
Cut formats that need a meal, a trip or another single-use setup per episode.
Keep formats like a packing-bench Q&A or a staff street interview.
Pilot the chosen format for a week before building a team or archive around it.

test.method: Pilot for 1 week and check impressions and sales before committing further resources.

title: Use speed as the hook when the buyer knows the normal pace
hypothesis: If content shows the product doing a familiar job faster than expected, then the gap between expected and actual time becomes the hook, provided the format is tagged so reads compare like with like.

signal.check: A category has a known normal pace (a 30-second routine, a 1-minute setup) that the store's content has never compressed for effect.

expected_effect.size: unknown; partly framed as an algorithm preference claim, not measured

risk.note: A format tagging and editing choice only.

steps: Identify a task with the product that has a known normal pace.
Film and edit it to show the product completing it faster than expected.
Tag the post as a 'speed' format so the read compares it only to other speed posts.

test.method: Compare hook_rate on speed-tagged posts against the account's speed-format baseline.

title: Build a signature set that doubles as merchandising
hypothesis: If the account builds a signature set around the product (a wall of stock, a fitting room, a workbench), then it compounds credibility and gives the feed a recognisable place, even though the set cannot rescue weak content on its own.

signal.check: The feed has no recognisable place or set the audience associates with the brand.

expected_effect.size: unknown; single-source example, no measured lift

risk.note: A one-off set investment; low ongoing risk.

steps: Decide the one signature place: a wall of product, a workshop, a workbench or a fitting room.
Build or buy the minimum set piece needed to make it recognisable.
Use the set consistently across posts in that pillar.
Keep content quality as the priority; the set alone will not rescue a weak post.

test.method: Track brand recall and comments referencing the set over a quarter.
test.read_point: After a quarter of consistent set use

title: Raise production stakes with a location change when talking-head content goes flat
hypothesis: If a flat talking-head format moves outdoors, into the warehouse or to the market, then engagement can recover because outcomes feel less scripted, without resorting to a dangerous stunt.

signal.check: Talking-head content at the same desk has been flat for several posts running.

expected_effect.size: unknown; craft claim, no lift given

risk.note: A location change only; avoid any dangerous stunt.

steps: Identify the flat talking-head format and its usual location.
Move filming outdoors, to the warehouse or the market for the next few posts.
Rule out any dangerous stunt as part of the change.
Compare engagement to the prior location.

test.method: Compare hold_rate before and after the location change.
test.read_point: After the next 3 posts in the new location

title: Set up 1 key light and practical background lights for every shoot
hypothesis: If every filming setup uses one key light and practical background lights instead of ambient room light, then the first frame reads as intentional even for raw or low-budget content.

signal.check: A shoot uses only ambient room light, or the first frame looks flat and unintentional.

risk.note: A setup change with a small, one-time equipment cost.

prerequisites: a window or a cheap softbox and a few lamps
steps: Turn off ambient room light.
Set one key light facing the subject: a large window or a cheap softbox.
Add practical background lights, such as lamps, for depth.
Choose a consistent set that fits the account's stance.
Compare before and after on the same phone camera to confirm it reads as deliberate.

test.method: Run the half-second screenshot test before and after the lighting change.
test.measure: pass rate on the screenshot test

expected_effect.size: unknown; craft claim, no lift given

title: Run the carousel path with more design when nobody will go on camera
hypothesis: If a faceless brand invests more in design and product photography for carousels, then visuals and craft can carry the credibility a person would otherwise provide.
does_not_apply_when: brands with a willing founder or named employee, who should run the personal-account path instead

signal.check: Nobody at the store is willing to go on camera and the current feed relies on generic stock-style images.

expected_effect.size: unknown; single-source claim, no measured lift

risk.note: A design-investment decision, reversible by changing the plan next month.

prerequisites: design and product photography capacity
steps: Confirm no one at the store will go on camera.
Increase investment in design and product photography for carousels.
Track carousel saves and PDP clicks per post as the read metric.

test.method: Track carousel saves and PDP clicks after increasing design investment.

title: Run every Reel through the SHARE checklist before publishing
hypothesis: If every Reel is checked for Simple, Hook, Authentic, Relatable and Entertaining before publishing, then weaker posts get caught and fixed before they go live.

signal.check: A Reel is ready to publish with no structured pre-publish check applied.

expected_effect.size: unknown; craft checklist, no lift given

risk.note: A pre-publish review step only.

steps: Check Simple: does it pass the drunk grandma test?
Check Hook: is it visually arresting with the product visible?
Check Authentic: is the idea-to-execution gap short, not over-edited?
Check Relatable: is it a specific buyer moment, not vague?
Check Entertaining: does the education ride inside an entertaining wrapper?
Hold the post if any of the 5 checks fail.

test.method: Track which SHARE checks fail most often across a month of posts.

title: Run a winning format for at least 8 weeks while keeping a second format live
hypothesis: If a winning format runs for at least 8 weeks and the account keeps at least 1 other format live at the same time, then the account gets the compounding benefit of consistency without depending on a single series.

signal.check: A winning format was swapped out after only a week or two, or the account depends on a single live format.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a merged rule between 2 conflicting sources, no shared number

risk.note: A cadence-commitment rule only.

prerequisites: a proven winning format from the monthly read
steps: Commit the winning format to the calendar for at least 8 weeks.
Keep at least 1 other format live in parallel.
Retire the winner only after the phase metric falls for 4 straight episodes.

test.method: Track the phase metric across the 8-week commitment and the parallel second format.

title: Give story-led videos a real ending: reveal, fix or offer
hypothesis: If a story-led video ends with the product reveal, the fix or the offer instead of stopping after the strong opening, then it becomes memorable instead of a missed chance to close the loop.
does_not_apply_when: speed-format posts, where compression itself is the point

signal.check: A story-led video stops right after the strong opening with no ending.

expected_effect.size: unknown; craft claim, no lift given

risk.note: A script-editing addition only.

steps: Read the last 3 lines of the story-led script.
Check for a payoff, reveal or resolved loop.
Add an ending row from the teardown grid if one is missing.

test.method: Compare completion and next-day recall on story posts with and without a clear ending.

title: Build a creator bench and shared footage archive before the founder becomes the ceiling
hypothesis: If the store hires for proven views, builds a shared footage archive, and pays editors a base plus a bonus, then output can grow past what the founder alone can film.
does_not_apply_when: accounts where the founder is not yet the output bottleneck

signal.check: The founder is the only creator and output is capped at about once a day.

expected_effect.size: one presenter's case: a 10,000-follower employee grew the brand account past 500,000; a single example, not a benchmark

risk.note: Editor output can drift from brand voice without a clear brief; tighten the brief before cutting the program.

prerequisites: founder confirmed as the output bottleneck
budget for editor pay
steps: Confirm the founder is the primary creator and output is capped.
Hire for proven views: an influencer, videographer or social manager who has had a video perform, or promote an employee who already posts.
Start a shared footage archive that founder, staff and family upload to continuously.
Recruit editors, give them the archive and examples, and pay a base rate plus a bonus for videos that go viral and convert.
Keep the founder supplying stories and positions even after the bench is built.

test.method: Track output volume and phase-metric performance before and after the bench is built.
test.read_point: 3 months after the bench is staffed

title: Diagnose a sales plateau as a founder-capacity ceiling before blaming the product
hypothesis: If a flat or falling-sales plateau with unchanged posting is checked against competitor entry and founder output first, then the team avoids wrongly blaming the product for a capacity problem.

signal.check: Sales are flat or falling with a founder-led account and unchanged posting volume.

expected_effect.size: unknown; diagnostic claim, no lift given

risk.note: A diagnostic read only.

prerequisites: 8 weeks of sales, post-date and impression data
steps: Check whether new competitors entered the category since the plateau started.
Check whether the founder still films everything at about once a day.
Run the business read: sales spikes against post dates, weekly sales in a strong-content week, discount codes, impressions.
If content works, post more; if not, fix the content before adding people.

test.method: Run the 8-week business read before deciding on product changes vs a bench build.
test.measure: sales by day vs post dates

title: Adapt length and cut per platform while keeping the product idea the same
hypothesis: If a cross-posted series keeps the same product idea but adapts length and cut per platform, then it can perform on each platform's norms without diluting the underlying message.

signal.check: A series is cross-posted with the exact same cut and length on every platform.

expected_effect.size: unknown; single example, no stated reason

risk.note: An editing variation only.

steps: Identify the core product idea that must stay constant.
Cut a shorter version for platforms that favor brevity.
Cut a longer version for platforms that support it.
Confirm the core idea is unchanged across versions.

test.method: Compare completion rate for each platform-length version.

title: Film the unboxing or packaging reveal as its own format
hypothesis: If a physical product with a considered unboxing moment gets its own unboxing-reveal format, then packaging becomes part of the story instead of a detail buried inside a founder story.
does_not_apply_when: products with no distinct packaging or unboxing moment

signal.check: A product has packaging the store designed with care but no dedicated unboxing content exists.

expected_effect.size: unknown; no library source, verify against brand data

risk.note: A format addition only.

prerequisites: a physical product with a designed unboxing moment
steps: Confirm the product has a considered unboxing or packaging reveal moment.
Film the box, the unwrap and the first look at the product.
Track saves and shares against the account's baseline for this format.

test.method: Compare saves and shares on unboxing posts to the account baseline.

title: Pick 1 hero platform by where actual buyers spend time, not presenter preference
hypothesis: If the hero platform is chosen from a small sample of actual or likely customers rather than presenter preference, then the account judges itself on the platform its buyers really use, which can differ by geography.

signal.check: The team is posting everywhere with no data-based read on which platform holds the most customers.

expected_effect.size: unknown; general practice for the geography branch

risk.note: A channel-focus decision, reversible after 6 months of data.

prerequisites: a small sample of customers or a proxy to survey
steps: Ask a small random sample of customers which platform they use most.
If a sample is not possible, use where the team itself learns about the category as a proxy.
Pick the densest platform and add email as the only other channel.
If TikTok and Instagram tie, run both as the base but read results on 1 for the verdict.
Commit to the choice for 6 months before adding a platform.

test.method: Compare organic_sessions and saves on the hero platform vs cross-posted platforms over 6 months.

title: Treat YouTube Shorts and side platforms as free reach with zero sales expectation
hypothesis: If cross-posts to LinkedIn, X or YouTube Shorts are treated as free reach with zero sales expectation unless someone will answer comments there, then the team avoids wasted effort chasing low-value views.

signal.check: The team spends meaningful time on a secondary platform with no plan to answer its comments or measure its sales.

expected_effect.size: unknown; one presenter's opinion that about 30,000 Shorts views 'doesn't really do much'

risk.note: An expectation-setting rule only.

steps: List the secondary platforms currently receiving cross-posts.
For each, confirm whether someone will answer comments there.
If not, keep the cross-post but set the sales expectation to zero.
Do not invest extra production time in platforms with no comment coverage.

test.method: Track whether secondary-platform effort correlates with any measurable sales or lead signal.

title: Default to a Creator account and use Business only when TikTok Shop needs it
hypothesis: If the store defaults to a Creator account on TikTok and Instagram, and only switches to Business when a TikTok Shop tie-in needs it, then the account avoids any distribution disadvantage tied to account type.

signal.check: The account setup and type per platform has not been checked or recorded.

expected_effect.size: unknown; single-source claim, verify current platform UI before acting

risk.note: An account settings change, reversible.

prerequisites: current platform documentation on account types, verified live
steps: Check current account type on each platform.
Default to Creator on TikTok and Instagram.
Switch to TikTok Business only when a TikTok Shop tie-in requires it.
Record the account type per platform in the account foundations document.

test.method: Confirm account type matches the rule after the setup review.
test.measure: account type recorded correctly per platform

title: Register and post the account from the country the store actually sells in
hypothesis: If the account is registered and posted from the store's target selling country, then distribution is not put at a disadvantage outside the US, Canada and English-speaking Europe.
does_not_apply_when: stores selling primarily in the US, Canada or English-speaking Europe

signal.check: The store sells in India, the Gulf or Europe but the account or founder is posting from elsewhere, or was set up while travelling.

expected_effect.size: unknown; single-source claim, verify current platform UI before acting

risk.note: Account registration country can be hard to change after the fact without support access issues.

prerequisites: a local contact or hire in the target country if nobody is currently there
steps: Check the account's registration country against the target market in the brand record.
If nobody is in-country, hire someone there to set up and post, with account access under the brand's control.
Never set up an account while travelling outside the target country.
Keep a backup of account access under brand, not personal, control.

test.method: Confirm registration country matches the target market at the account audit.
test.read_point: At account setup and each audit

title: Spin a proven format into a satellite account only after it wins on the main account
hypothesis: If a satellite account is only started once a format has proven strong enough to carry its own feed, and the team can hold both posting floors, then a drop in performance is easier to diagnose than mixing everything on one account.
does_not_apply_when: accounts that have not yet proven a format on the main feed

signal.check: The team is considering a satellite account (a tips account, a testimonials account) before any format has proven itself on the main account.

expected_effect.size: unknown; hypothetical structure, no measured lift

risk.note: A second account adds ongoing capacity load; can be shut down if it underperforms.

prerequisites: a proven format on the main account
confirmed capacity to hold both posting floors
steps: Confirm the format has proven itself on the main account's monthly read.
Check the team can hold the posting floor on both the main and satellite account.
Start with at most 1 satellite account.
Keep the main account as the sandbox for testing new formats.

test.method: Track posting floor adherence and phase-metric performance on both accounts after launch.

title: Keep the product's visual world consistent across every platform
hypothesis: If colours, set, packaging and story stay consistent across platforms instead of each looking different, then a buyer meeting the store on a second platform feels a second discovery that reinforces the first.

signal.check: The account's visual style differs noticeably between platforms with no shared colours, set or packaging cues.

expected_effect.size: unknown; craft claim, no lift given

risk.note: A style-guide alignment task.

prerequisites: a documented visual style guide
steps: Document the account's colours, set and packaging cues.
Compare current posts on each platform against the style guide.
Fix any platform whose visuals have drifted from the shared style.

test.method: Audit visual consistency across platforms quarterly.
test.measure: share of posts matching the style guide

title: Post manually for 4 weeks, then test a scheduler against manual posting
hypothesis: If the team posts manually for a 4-week baseline, then runs alternating manual and scheduled weeks with the same pillar mix, then the brand gets its own answer on whether a scheduler hurts reach instead of relying on an unverified claim.

signal.check: The team is about to buy or already uses a scheduler with no brand-specific test on file.

expected_effect.size: 1 presenter's internal test over 'hundreds of videos' with no method shown; unverified

risk.note: Easy to revert to manual posting if the scheduled weeks underperform.

prerequisites: 4 weeks of manual posting baseline
steps: Post manually for 4 weeks as the baseline, budgeting 2 to 3 minutes per platform.
Alternate manual and scheduled weeks with the same pillar mix.
Log non-follower reach, retention and shares per post for each week type.
Compare the 2 conditions in code and record the result in the experiment log.
Adopt whichever the brand's own data supports.

test.method: Compare non-follower reach across manual vs scheduled weeks over 2 alternating cycles.

title: Move restocks, codes and CTAs to Stories once followers exist
hypothesis: If restocks, discount codes, links and CTAs move to Stories once a meaningful follower base exists, then the account uses the format that followers actually see, instead of wasting Story production on a new account.
does_not_apply_when: new accounts with no meaningful follower base yet

signal.check: The account has followers but still runs CTAs, codes and restock alerts only through feed posts, not Stories.

expected_effect.size: unknown; craft claim, no lift given

risk.note: A channel-shift decision only.

prerequisites: a meaningful follower base
steps: Confirm the account has enough followers for Story views to be meaningful.
Move restock alerts, discount codes, links and hard CTAs to Stories.
Track Story views and link taps in the monthly read.

test.method: Track Story views and link taps against feed-post CTA performance.

title: Use native shoppable tags on Instagram and Facebook, not just TikTok Shop
hypothesis: If products are tagged directly in Instagram and Facebook posts and Reels wherever the platform supports it, then buyers get a shorter path to the PDP than relying on TikTok Shop alone.

signal.check: The store has a synced product catalogue but posts on Instagram or Facebook carry no native product tags.

expected_effect.size: unknown; largely general practice beyond the TikTok Shop tie-in, verify current features

risk.note: A setup task using existing native platform features.

prerequisites: a synced product catalogue on the relevant platforms
steps: Confirm the catalogue is synced to Instagram and Facebook.
Tag the featured SKU directly in each eligible post and Reel.
Check the tagged product matches the SKU shown and the live PDP price.

test.method: Compare cvr_pdp_to_cart on tagged posts vs untagged posts of the same format.

title: Set the CTA-free window and view threshold by the store's price point
hypothesis: If a new account runs month 1 with no CTA, then adds keyword lead-magnet CTAs on 1 to 2 posts a week from month 2 while low-AOV stores can move faster than high-AOV or considered-purchase stores, then reach builds before it is spent on early hard sells.
does_not_apply_when: stores that need leads immediately and cannot wait for a threshold

signal.check: An owner asks when posts can start saying 'shop now', or CTAs already appear before any traction.

expected_effect.size: 1 presenter's threshold is about 5,000 views (about 2,000 in narrow niches); disputed by other sources, see the CTA conflict

risk.note: Early hard CTAs can suppress non-follower reach; watch it for 4 weeks after any change.

prerequisites: the store's price ladder
a mid-funnel asset (see lead magnet idea)
steps: Run month 1 with no CTA at all on a new account.
From month 2, add keyword lead-magnet CTAs on 1 to 2 posts a week, even below any view threshold.
Reserve hard sells for bottom-funnel posts and for Stories once followers exist.
Watch non-follower reach for 4 weeks after any CTA layer change.
For a low-AOV store, move faster; for high-AOV or considered purchase, wait longer and route to a call.

test.method: Track non-follower reach for 4 weeks after the CTA layer goes live.
test.read_point: 4 weeks after the CTA layer starts

title: Replace 'link in bio' with a comment keyword that DMs the buyer directly
hypothesis: If a comment keyword triggers a DM with the PDP link, size guide or code instead of routing to 'link in bio', then more engaged viewers convert because they stay on the post and get a personal notification.

signal.check: A post's only CTA is 'link in bio' and comment or DM volume is low relative to views.

expected_effect.size: unknown; 4 sources claim it, no shared number

risk.note: Depends on a DM automation tool and current Meta messaging policy; check both before launch.

prerequisites: a DM automation tool with confirmed policy status
a lead magnet or destination link ready
steps: Choose a DM automation tool and confirm its current approved-partner status.
Set up the flow: a comment containing the keyword triggers a DM with the link, guide or code.
State the keyword on screen and in the caption.
Test the flow end to end with 2 team accounts before the post goes live.

test.method: Track DM opens and clicks per keyword after launch.
test.read_point: Weekly after the flow goes live

title: Use 1 distinct keyword per campaign or SKU for clean attribution
hypothesis: If each campaign or SKU gets its own distinct comment keyword, then DMs and sales can be mapped back to the exact post and offer that drove them.

signal.check: Several posts share the same generic keyword, such as 'LINK', making attribution impossible.

expected_effect.size: unknown; process rule, no lift given

risk.note: A naming convention change only.

prerequisites: the DM automation tool from the comment-to-DM idea
steps: Assign 1 distinct keyword per campaign or SKU.
State the keyword on screen and in the caption.
Map each keyword to sales in the DM tool export.

test.method: Check keyword-to-sales mapping accuracy monthly.

title: Attach a lead magnet to only 1 or 2 posts a week
hypothesis: If a lead magnet appears on only 1 or 2 posts a week instead of every post, then the CTA stays fresh and the account avoids looking like it is selling on every post.

signal.check: Every post ends with 'comment GUIDE' or a similar lead-magnet CTA.

expected_effect.size: unknown; single-source claim, no measured lift

risk.note: A frequency cap only.

prerequisites: the lead magnet and DM flow already set up
steps: Count how many posts this week carry the lead-magnet CTA.
Cap it to 1 or 2 posts a week.
Rotate which post carries it based on the calendar's funnel-stage plan.

test.method: Compare non-follower reach on weeks with capped lead-magnet frequency vs uncapped.
test.read_point: After 4 weeks at the capped frequency

title: Match the lead magnet to something the buyer actually wants
hypothesis: If the lead magnet is a size guide, care guide or first-order code the buyer actually wants, and a mid-funnel asset exists before any hard offer, then it keeps producing leads for months instead of a quick drop-off.

signal.check: A lead magnet is planned or live with no clear match to what the store's buyer actually wants, or no mid-funnel asset exists yet.

expected_effect.size: one presenter's well-matched freebie kept producing leads for 6 to 8 months; own account only

risk.note: Can be swapped for a different resource if it underperforms.

prerequisites: knowledge of what the store's customer actually wants as a free resource
steps: Identify a free resource the buyer genuinely wants: a size guide, care guide or first-order code.
Confirm a simple mid-funnel asset (newsletter, waitlist, buying guide) exists before any hard offer.
Track claims per post and the share that later buy.

test.method: Track lead-magnet claim rate and later purchase rate over the following weeks.

title: Send a thank-you-only DM on a new follow, with no pitch or code
hypothesis: If the automated new-follow DM says thanks with no pitch or code, then the account avoids reading as spammy while still opening a channel.

signal.check: The new-follow DM includes a pitch, a discount code or a hard sell.

expected_effect.size: unknown; single-source claim, no measured lift

risk.note: A message-content change only.

prerequisites: a DM automation tool
steps: Turn on the new-follow DM with a thank-you-only message.
Remove any pitch, code or hard sell from it.
Plan for inbox batching if the message volume grows large at scale.

test.method: Check the new-follow DM text against the rule at every audit.
test.measure: pass or fail on the message content check

title: Follow up in DM with buyers who clicked the link but did not order
hypothesis: If a short, time-boxed personal message goes to buyers who clicked the product link but did not order, then some of that near-miss demand converts instead of being lost.

signal.check: DM automation analytics show clicks well above orders, with no follow-up message built.

expected_effect.size: 1 presenter's own example: 10 clicked, 3 bought, 7 identifiable to follow up; not a benchmark

risk.note: Must stay inside current platform messaging window rules.

prerequisites: DM automation analytics tracking clicks and orders
steps: Identify buyers who clicked the product link but did not order.
Send a short, time-boxed personal message referencing their interest and any deadline.
Keep the message inside current platform messaging window rules.
Log orders that result from the follow-up.

test.method: Track orders attributable to the follow-up message vs the clicked-not-bought pool.
test.read_point: Weekly after the follow-up flow is live

title: Test the DM funnel end to end before any triggering post goes live
hypothesis: If the DM automation flow is tested end to end and connected to the store's email or SMS list before a triggering post goes live, then a broken link or dead code does not waste a viral spike.

signal.check: A post that triggers a DM flow is about to go live with no end-to-end test done.

expected_effect.size: unknown; QA claim, no lift given

risk.note: A broken flow during a spike wastes the spike but can be fixed for the next post.

prerequisites: the DM automation flow built
steps: Test the flow with 2 team accounts before the post goes live.
Confirm the DM lands, the link works and any code applies at checkout.
Connect the flow to the store's email or SMS destination.
Confirm intake capacity: who answers replies, who fulfils.

test.method: Run the end-to-end test before every post carrying a DM automation trigger.
test.measure: pass or fail on the end-to-end test

title: Answer every comment and DM fast with a specific reply and a next step
hypothesis: If every comment and DM gets a fast, specific reply plus a next step (a code, a size guide, a PDP link), then more buyers move forward instead of losing interest waiting for an answer.

signal.check: A product question like 'is this available in blue' sits unanswered for a day or more.

expected_effect.size: unknown; craft claim, no lift given

risk.note: A response-process change only.

prerequisites: a named inbox owner
steps: Assign a named owner to comments and DMs each day.
Reply to every comment with a specific answer, not 'thanks!'.
Reply to every DM personally.
When a product question appears, DM the answer plus a next step: a code, a size guide or a booking link.
Also comment on other accounts' posts in the niche on the hero platform.

test.method: Track median reply time and unanswered comment count.

title: Sell low-ticket in-app; route high-ticket or considered purchases to a call
hypothesis: If low-ticket products and free lead magnets sell inside the app while high-ticket or considered purchases route to a call, consultation or fitting, then each price tier gets the closing process it needs.

signal.check: A high-ticket or considered-purchase product is being closed directly in DMs with no booking step.

expected_effect.size: unknown; no source gives a price cutoff, needs brand data

risk.note: A routing rule only.

prerequisites: the store's price ladder from the brand record
steps: Mark each SKU on the price ladder as low-ticket or high-ticket or considered.
For low-ticket SKUs, keep the sale inside the app or DM.
For high-ticket or considered SKUs, insert a booking step for a call, consultation or fitting.
Record the routing on the calendar row for each post.

test.method: Track close rate and AOV by routing path.

title: Send every post's next step to a live, matching PDP or landing page
hypothesis: If every post's hard or soft CTA points to a PDP or landing page that is live and matches the SKU shown, then attention does not leak to a dead link or a mismatched product page.

signal.check: A post's CTA destination is not confirmed live, or the linked SKU does not match the one shown in the post.

expected_effect.size: unknown; process claim, no lift given

risk.note: A pre-publish check only.

steps: Confirm the destination page is live before the post publishes.
Confirm the destination SKU matches the SKU shown in the post.
Check stock and price are current on the destination page.

test.method: Audit destination links before every publish.
test.measure: pass rate on the destination check

title: Route every CTA to owned destinations, never to another social platform
hypothesis: If every CTA points only to the store's email, SMS list or private community, and never to another social platform, then the account builds a durable owned asset instead of losing the audience to a platform it does not control.

signal.check: A caption or Story includes 'watch my YouTube' or a raw URL pointing to another social platform.

expected_effect.size: unknown; craft claim, no lift given

risk.note: A copy-editing rule only.

steps: Scan every caption and Story for outbound social links or cross-platform call-outs.
Remove any that route to another social platform.
Replace with a keyword, bio link or Story link to an owned destination: email, SMS or community.

test.method: Audit captions for outbound social links before every publish.
test.measure: pass rate on the outbound-link check

title: Set a launch cadence of continuous lead magnets plus 1 to 2 launches a year
hypothesis: If the promo calendar runs continuous lead magnets with 1 or 2 real product launches a year plus seasonal sales, then the calendar has a steady lead engine instead of relying only on occasional big moments.

signal.check: The promo calendar has no continuous lead-magnet cadence, or launch slots are not tied to real drop dates and stock.

expected_effect.size: unknown; single-source claim, no measured lift

risk.note: A calendar planning change only.

prerequisites: real launch and stock dates
steps: Set a continuous lead-magnet cadence in the calendar.
Add 1 to 2 real product launches a year, tied to real drop dates and stock.
Layer seasonal sales on top of the continuous lead-magnet content.

test.method: Track list growth and sales lift around launch and seasonal slots.
test.read_point: Around each launch and quarterly overall

title: Reuse every content asset across the PDP, email, DM and post-purchase surfaces
hypothesis: If every winning content asset is reused on the PDP, in a pre-purchase email, in a DM answer and in a post-purchase follow-up, then one piece of work pays off across the whole buyer path instead of being spent once.

signal.check: A winning asset has a reuse list covering fewer than 2 store surfaces.

expected_effect.size: unknown; process claim, no lift given

risk.note: A repurposing task only.

prerequisites: a confirmed winning asset
steps: Confirm the asset is a proven winner from the monthly read.
Write a reuse list naming at least 2 store surfaces: PDP, email, DM or post-purchase.
Adapt the asset for each surface without changing the underlying claim.
Route email and SMS steps to 14-EML.

test.method: Track engagement or conversion on each surface after reuse.
test.read_point: After each surface adaptation goes live

title: Turn stock status into content: restocks, low-stock framing and waitlists
hypothesis: If a hero SKU about to sell out or just restocked gets a dedicated post using true stock counts, then real scarcity converts more than a generic post, without ever claiming false low stock.
does_not_apply_when: stores with no real stock constraints or drop-based launches

signal.check: A hero SKU is about to sell out or has just restocked with no content planned around it.

expected_effect.size: unknown; no library source, verify against brand data

risk.note: Claiming false scarcity risks trust and platform or legal exposure; stock counts must be real.

prerequisites: current stock counts from the inventory system
steps: Pull the current stock count for the SKU from the inventory system.
Post the restock announcement, or a waitlist opener ahead of a drop.
Never state a stock level that is not true.
Track orders against the post.

test.method: Compare orders in the hours after the stock-status post to a normal day.

title: Offer a bundle or higher-tier product in CTA content, not only the entry item
hypothesis: If a store with more than 1 price point offers a bundle or a higher-tier upgrade in some CTA content instead of always the entry item, then average order value from content-driven sales can rise.
does_not_apply_when: single-price-point stores

signal.check: Every CTA routes to the entry-level item even though the store has bundles or higher-tier products available.

expected_effect.size: unknown; no library source, verify against brand data

risk.note: A CTA-routing change; bundle logic itself is designed in 03-OFF.

prerequisites: a defined bundle or upgrade path from 03-OFF
steps: Identify a returning or engaged audience segment for the post.
Route its CTA or keyword code to a bundle or upgrade offer instead of the entry item.
Track AOV on orders from that code or keyword against the store's overall AOV.

test.method: Compare AOV on bundle-routed CTA orders to the store's overall AOV.
test.read_point: After the next month of bundle-routed CTAs

title: Reuse a sales-moving post at least 4 times with a changed wrapper
hypothesis: If a post that moved real sales, not just views, gets reused at least 4 times with a new hook, a carousel version, a voiceover version and a platform-length cut, then one proven story keeps earning instead of being made once and dropped.
does_not_apply_when: posts that only moved views, with no confirmed sales lift

signal.check: A post with a confirmed sales lift has never been reused in a different wrapper.

expected_effect.size: unknown; craft claim, no lift given

risk.note: Stop at the first version that fails to move the phase metric.

prerequisites: confirmation the asset moved sales, from the business read
steps: Confirm the win on the business read: impressions and sales, not only views.
Make version 2: a new hook on the same body.
Make version 3: a text carousel built from the script.
Make version 4: an AI voiceover or new footage, with a disclosure check.
Space versions across weeks and recheck impressions and sales after each before making the next.

test.method: Track impressions and sales after each reuse version.

title: Reuse a story across brand-controlled accounts only with a different wrapper
hypothesis: If a proven story is reused across a brand account and a founder or fan account with a different angle and wrapper each time, then it compounds without reading as duplicate content.
does_not_apply_when: a single-account brand with no second brand-controlled account

signal.check: The same story or near-duplicate post is planned across 2 or more brand-controlled accounts on the same platform.

expected_effect.size: unknown; disputed by general platform guidance on duplicate content, unverified

risk.note: Near-duplicate content across accounts may conflict with platform policy; check before doing it.

prerequisites: a second brand-controlled account
current platform policy on duplicate content checked
steps: Confirm the story has already worked once on the primary account.
Write a different angle, wrapper or named voice for the second account.
Check current platform policy on duplicate or near-duplicate content before publishing.
Never post a near-identical copy to a second account.

test.method: Compare reach on the second-account version to the primary account's original.

title: Feed one deep piece into many store surfaces
hypothesis: If one deep piece, such as a buying guide or a founder interview, is broken into shorts, carousels, PDP copy, email and ad creative, then the production time behind it pays off across many surfaces instead of one post.

signal.check: A long buying guide, founder interview or sourcing documentary exists but has only been used once, in one format.

expected_effect.size: unknown; process claim, no lift given

risk.note: A repurposing task only.

prerequisites: the remix machinery: an approved story set and voice guide
steps: Identify the deep piece and its core claims and story beats.
Cut it into shorts and carousels adapted per platform.
Pull nuance into PDP copy, email and ad creative drafts.
Write the reuse list for the piece before spending more production time on it.

test.method: Track how many surfaces the deep piece eventually fed.
test.read_point: 1 quarter after the piece is made

title: Mark a well-told story approved and reuse the exact line
hypothesis: If a story that landed well in the monthly read gets marked approved, then the exact line can be reused across formats and platforms for years instead of being rewritten from scratch each time.

signal.check: A story performed well in the monthly read but is not marked approved in the story set.

expected_effect.size: one presenter reused an opening line hundreds of times over 5 to 10 years; own case only

risk.note: A tagging task only.

prerequisites: the story set from the story-mining idea
steps: Identify a story that landed well in the monthly read.
Mark it approved in the story set.
Reuse the exact line across formats and platforms.
Keep personality content on the named person's account, not the brand handle.

test.method: Track reuse count and performance of the approved story over time.

title: Retire launch and sale posts after their window; never resurface a dated post
hypothesis: If launch, sale and trend posts are retired after their window and never resurfaced, then the account avoids showing customers a stale or expired offer.

signal.check: A dated launch or sale post is still live, pinned or being reshared after its window closed.

expected_effect.size: unknown; craft claim, no lift given

risk.note: A cleanup task only.

prerequisites: the timely or timeless label on every post
steps: List all timely-labelled posts and their windows.
Retire or archive any post past its window.
Do not resurface a dated post; make a fresh timeless version instead if the underlying idea is worth keeping.

test.method: Audit the feed monthly for expired timely posts still visible.
test.measure: count of expired posts still live

title: Only commission a content library with a distribution plan already in place
hypothesis: If the channels and workflow for using a photo library, UGC bundle or video series are written down before spending, then the purchase pays off instead of sitting unused for lack of distribution machinery.

signal.check: A proposal to buy a photo library, UGC bundle or video series exists with no written distribution plan.

expected_effect.size: unknown; craft claim, no lift given

risk.note: An unused purchase wastes budget; catching this before the purchase order avoids it.

steps: Write down the channels the content will feed: feed, PDP, email, ads.
Write the workflow for who pulls from it and how often.
Confirm the plan exists before the purchase order is signed.

test.method: Check usage rate of the purchased library 90 days after buying it.

title: Keep categorised swipe files split by DTC competitor vs non-retail sources
hypothesis: If swipe files are split by DTC competitor ads vs non-retail sources and pulled from before writing, then structure borrowed from a non-retail source never gets applied unchanged to a physical product's PDP.

signal.check: The swipe file is unsorted, or a writer starts a batch with a blank page and no swipe file to pull from.

expected_effect.size: unknown; craft claim, no lift given

risk.note: A filing task only.

steps: Split the swipe file into DTC competitor entries and non-competitor entries (banks, software, media).
For hooks, further split by the 15 hook types.
Record on-screen text, spoken words, audio and visual together per entry, with a date.
Pull 2 or 3 entries before writing and riff on structure only.

test.method: Check the swipe file has the split and dated entries at the next batch day.
test.measure: presence of the split and dates

title: Never paste swiped wording into a caption, PDP or ad
hypothesis: If swiped wording never gets pasted directly into a caption, PDP or ad, then the brand avoids legal and originality risk while still using swipe files for structure.

signal.check: A draft contains wording lifted directly from a swipe file entry rather than rewritten in the brand's own words.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a compliance rule, no lift given

risk.note: Pasted wording found in a published piece can bring legal and brand risk.

steps: Compare the draft to its swipe-file source.
Flag and rewrite any directly lifted phrase.
Confirm only structure, not wording, was borrowed.

test.method: Run the compliance check comparing drafts to swipe sources before publishing.

title: Tear down a winning video with the beginning-middle-end grid
hypothesis: If a winning video (a competitor's, an out-of-niche winner, or the brand's own top or bottom post) is torn down with a grid covering location, cuts, audio, text, lighting and viewer emotion at each stage, then the brand can rebuild the structure with its own content.

signal.check: A strong competitor, out-of-niche or internal post has never been torn down into a structural grid.

expected_effect.size: unknown; craft method, no lift given

risk.note: Only structure transfers; copying the source's words, footage or product creates legal risk.

steps: Watch the video once straight through.
Build the grid: rows for beginning, middle, end; columns for location, cuts and pacing, audio and trigger words, on-screen text, lighting, and viewer emotion.
Watch again and fill every cell with the concrete choice at that stage.
Optionally transcribe and ask AI where the hook lands, pacing slows, or a viewer would drop off.
Rebuild the structural choices with the brand's own product, story and script.
Run the same grid monthly on the brand's own top 3 and bottom 3 posts.

test.method: Compare completion and saves on the rebuilt piece vs the account baseline.

title: Do the first competitive format research by hand with 3 buyer phrases
hypothesis: If the first round of competitive research is done by hand using the 3 broadest phrases a buyer would type, then the idea bank starts with real judgment about what already works, before any research tool is used.

signal.check: The idea bank is being set up and no manual search pass has been logged.

expected_effect.size: unknown; process claim, no lift given

risk.note: A research task only.

prerequisites: the 3 broadest buyer search phrases for the category
steps: Search the 3 broadest buyer phrases (not brand names) on Instagram.
Scroll well past the first screen and note posts with unusually high views for their size.
Repeat on TikTok and YouTube, noting adjacent phrases those platforms suggest.
Re-search the adjacent phrases on Instagram.
Log topic, exact hook line, hook type, format and pace per post in a sheet.

test.method: Count new idea-bank lines produced from the manual research pass.

title: Track hook type against post performance and SKU over time
hypothesis: If every post is logged with its hook type and framing against its performance and SKU, then the monthly read can show which hook types actually work for this brand instead of guessing.

signal.check: The hooks bank has no performance results logged against hook type.

expected_effect.size: unknown; tracking claim, no lift given

risk.note: A tracking task, any spreadsheet works.

prerequisites: hook type tags on every post
steps: Log hook type and framing for every post in the hooks bank.
Record its performance results once published.
Read hook-type performance monthly, split by SKU.

test.method: Compare hook_rate by hook type in the monthly read.

title: Study the store's flops as deliberately as its winners
hypothesis: If flops get the same structured study as winners every month, then the do-not-do list catches real patterns instead of the team skipping the review because it hurts.

signal.check: The monthly read has no flop list, or flops are dismissed without analysis.

expected_effect.size: unknown; framed as valuable data by multiple sources, no shared lift number

risk.note: An analysis step only.

prerequisites: post-level performance data
steps: Identify the bottom 5 posts by the phase metric each month.
Run the teardown grid on the weakest posts.
Write the patterns into a do-not-do list.
Feed the do-not-do list into next month's calendar planning.

test.method: Track whether do-not-do patterns recur in the following month's flops.

title: Judge a format over weeks and several SKUs, never by 1 post
hypothesis: If a format is judged only after at least 4 posts, then a single flop or single hit does not drive a strategy change based on noise.

signal.check: An owner is reacting to 1 flop or 1 hit as if it were a verdict on the whole format.

expected_effect.size: unknown; 4 sources agree on the pattern, no shared number

risk.note: A decision discipline rule only.

steps: Count posts run for the format in question.
If fewer than 4, hold off on any verdict.
At 4 or more, read the results and decide whether to continue, adjust or retire the format.

test.method: Track how many format decisions were made with fewer than 4 posts of data.

title: Build 3 top lists plus a flop list, each showing the SKU featured
hypothesis: If the monthly read builds top lists for views, followers gained and deep engagement plus a flop list, each showing the SKU featured, then recurring winning formats and patterns become visible instead of judging posts one at a time.

signal.check: The monthly read has no structured top or flop lists tied to SKU.

expected_effect.size: unknown; process claim, no lift given

risk.note: A reporting structure only.

prerequisites: post-level export with SKU tags
steps: Build a top-views list, a top-followers-gained list, and a top-comments-or-deep-engagement list, each with the SKU shown.
Build a flop list with the SKU shown.
Expect the lists to differ; expand formats that recur across the first 2 lists.
Write a do-not-do list from the flops.

test.method: Check whether recurring formats across the top lists get more calendar slots next month.

title: Read retention and 3-second watch rate per SKU, not just per post
hypothesis: If retention and the 3-second watch rate are read per SKU featured, not just per post, then the team learns which products the content actually builds demand for.

signal.check: The performance read reports retention and watch rate only at the post level, with no SKU breakdown.

expected_effect.size: unknown; general practice for the SKU-level read, verify against brand data

risk.note: A reporting structure change only.

prerequisites: SKU tags on every calendar row and post
steps: Add a SKU column to the post-level export.
Read retention and 3-second watch rate grouped by SKU.
Label the period growth or selling phase and read shares (growth) or comments and Story views (selling) accordingly.

test.method: Compare SKU-level retention across the monthly reads.

title: Measure completion, saves, comments, replays and CTR in a test round, not raw views
hypothesis: If a round of variant posts is measured on completion, saves, comments, replays, CTR and cost per lead instead of raw views or followers, then the test reveals which variant actually works, not just which one got seen.

signal.check: A variant test round is being judged on raw views or follower count instead of completion, saves and CTR.

expected_effect.size: unknown; process claim, no lift given

risk.note: A measurement-design change only.

prerequisites: several variants of one idea ready to publish
steps: Set the test metrics before the round starts: completion rate, saves, comments, replays, CTR to the PDP and cost per lead.
Publish the variants in a short window, ideally at the same time, to limit time-of-day effects.
Read the round on the pre-set metrics, not raw views or followers.

test.method: Compare the pre-set metrics across variants after the round.

title: Flag stranger-blind content when follower share of views tops 70 to 80%
hypothesis: If follower share of views is checked and flagged whenever it tops 70% to 80% with flat reach, then the last 5 to 10 posts get audited for inside references before growth stalls further.

signal.check: Follower share of views is at or above about 70% to 80% with flat overall reach.

expected_effect.size: one presenter's client pattern; own account example, not a benchmark

risk.note: A diagnostic read only.

prerequisites: follower vs non-follower view data
steps: Check follower share of views per post in the monthly read.
Flag any post at or above 70% to 80% with flat reach.
Audit the last 5 to 10 posts against the stranger-first writing rule.
Rewrite openers going forward to name the product plainly.

test.method: Recheck follower share after the next 5 posts.

title: Audit the last 20 videos for topic and buyer consistency before blaming content quality
hypothesis: If the last 20 videos are audited for topic and buyer consistency before touching content quality, then the team fixes the real problem, because scattered targeting looks like weak content but is not.

signal.check: Growth is weak on the account and the team is about to rework scripts or editing without first checking topic consistency.

expected_effect.size: unknown; diagnostic claim, no lift given

risk.note: A diagnostic audit only.

steps: List the last 20 videos with their topic and target buyer.
Check whether all 20 point at the same product topic and buyer.
If yes and growth is still weak, the fix is script, editing or value, not targeting.
If no, fix topic consistency (see the topic-focus idea) before touching content quality.

test.method: Track growth after the fix chosen by the audit result.
test.read_point: 1 month after the fix is applied

title: Tie content to sales with simple checks computed in code
hypothesis: If sales spikes are compared against post dates, week-on-week sales, impressions and discount-code redemptions using code rather than manual arithmetic, then the monthly read shows whether content actually moves sales.

signal.check: The monthly read has no business tie to sales, or the math is done by hand instead of in code.

expected_effect.size: unknown; process claim, no lift given

risk.note: A reporting build; missing values must show as unavailable, not zero.

prerequisites: sales by day, impressions by post, discount-code redemptions
steps: Pull sales by day, impressions by post, and discount-code redemptions used only in content.
Compare sales spikes to post dates in code.
Compare week-on-week sales in a week with several strong posts to a normal week.
Break sales down by SKU or collection featured, keeping totals separate from breakdowns.
Show missing values as unavailable, never as zero.
For a cleaner read, consider running the same organic post as a paid test, routed to 24-DEP.

test.method: Run the coded business-tie report each month and check for arithmetic done by hand.

title: Track leads per post and which keywords convert to orders, not just reply volume
hypothesis: If leads per post are tracked by keyword all the way to orders, not just DM reply volume, then the team learns which comment-to-DM campaigns actually make money.

signal.check: DM automation is live but reports only reply volume, with no keyword-to-order mapping.

expected_effect.size: unknown; tracking claim, no lift given

risk.note: A tracking build only.

prerequisites: the DM automation backend export
steps: Pull leads per post and per keyword from the DM tool export.
Map each keyword to any resulting order.
Read the keyword-to-order mapping monthly, not just reply counts.

test.method: Compare keyword conversion rates monthly.

title: Run the next-day recall check alongside the numbers when picking a concept
hypothesis: If the next-day recall check runs alongside the metric read when choosing between concepts, then a high-view idea with nothing memorable behind it does not automatically win.

signal.check: A concept decision is being made on metrics alone with no recall check run.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a tiebreaker heuristic, not a measured lift

risk.note: A decision-process addition only.

steps: Run the metric read on the competing concepts first.
Run the next-day recall test on the team's top 10 candidates.
Use recall as the tiebreaker when metrics are close, never as a replacement for them.

test.method: Track whether recall-favored concepts also perform on metrics after publishing.

title: Check the next 3 posts after any unusually broad hit for on-target reach
hypothesis: If the 3 posts after an unusually broad hit are checked for whether reach held inside the buyer slice, then the team can tell whether the hit helped or introduced noise into future targeting.

signal.check: A post far above baseline reach has not been followed by a check on the next 3 posts' performance.

expected_effect.size: unknown; diagnostic claim, no lift given

risk.note: A monitoring step only.

steps: Identify any post with reach well above baseline.
Track saves, DMs and PDP clicks vs baseline for that post.
Watch the next 3 posts to see whether reach held or dropped.
If reach dropped, return to on-target content.

test.method: Compare the next 3 posts' reach to the pre-hit baseline.
test.read_point: Within 2 weeks of the broad hit

title: Set the store's own engagement baseline instead of chasing an outside number
hypothesis: If the store sets its own baseline for retention, shares and engagement from its first 3 months, then CTA timing and performance verdicts are judged against real data instead of an invented 'good' number no source actually gives.

signal.check: The team is asking what a 'good' engagement rate is with no store-specific baseline recorded yet.

expected_effect.size: no source gives a number; needs the brand's own first-3-months data

risk.note: A measurement task only.

prerequisites: 3 months of consistent posting data
steps: Collect retention, shares and engagement data from the first 3 months of consistent posting.
Compute the store's own baseline from that data.
Use this baseline, not an outside number, for future CTA timing and verdicts.

test.method: Compare future months' performance against the store's own baseline.

title: Track uploads against the floor as the sole KPI in the first phase
hypothesis: If the first phase of a new or restarted account tracks only uploads against the floor, not sales, then the team avoids reacting to sales noise before the content itself has had a fair test.

signal.check: A new or restarted account's first-phase report includes sales figures instead of only uploads vs floor.

expected_effect.size: unknown; input-metric claim, no lift given

risk.note: A reporting change only.

steps: Confirm the account is in its first phase (months 1 to 3).
Report only uploads vs floor for this phase.
Hold sales-based judgments until the first macro read.

test.method: Review the weekly upload report through the first phase.

title: Confirm the link, stock and price are ready before a high-performing post publishes
hypothesis: If every post's matching PDP or collection link, stock and price are confirmed ready before it goes live, then attention converts at the product layer instead of hitting an out-of-stock or mismatched page.

signal.check: A post about to publish has no destination link ready, or its PDP is out of stock.

expected_effect.size: unknown; craft claim, no lift given

risk.note: A pre-publish check only.

steps: Confirm the link, stock and price for the calendar row before it goes live.
Hold the post if the PDP is out of stock or the price is stale.
Log the confirmed link, stock and price on the calendar row.

test.method: Audit the confirmed-ready checklist before every publish.
test.measure: pass rate on the pre-publish check

title: Build the brand's own list from organic reach instead of relying on sponsorships
hypothesis: If organic reach routes to building the store's own email or SMS list instead of chasing brand-deal sponsorships, then revenue comes from the product the brand already sells, not a separate media business.

signal.check: The brand account is being offered or is pursuing paid sponsorship deals as part of its content plan.

expected_effect.size: unknown; craft claim, no lift given

risk.note: A strategic-focus decision only.

steps: Confirm the brand account's content routes to the store's own list growth, not a sponsor's message.
Decline or deprioritise brand-deal sponsorships for the main store account.
For a founder's personal account, treat sponsorships as a separate decision that must not dilute topic discipline or voice.
Track list growth per month in the read.

test.method: Track list growth per month against content volume.

title: Route viral spikes to the mid-funnel asset, never straight to a hard pitch
hypothesis: If a viral post with no next step routes new attention to the mid-funnel asset instead of a hard pitch, then the reach converts into a lead instead of being pure vanity.

signal.check: A viral post has no lead magnet, list sign-up or mid-funnel asset behind it.

expected_effect.size: unknown; craft claim, no lift given

risk.note: A routing decision only.

prerequisites: a live mid-funnel asset (see the lead magnet idea)
steps: Confirm the mid-funnel asset is live before the next big post could go viral.
Route any viral spike's CTA to that mid-funnel asset.
Avoid a hard pitch on a post with no prior traction context.

test.method: Track lead capture rate from viral spikes with the mid-funnel asset live.

title: Use a content-only discount code as a simple attribution signal
hypothesis: If a discount code is named only in content, then its redemptions give a simple, clean attribution signal for that content, though it is not itself a discount strategy.

signal.check: Content has no dedicated tracking code, making its sales contribution invisible.

expected_effect.size: unknown; process claim, no lift given

risk.note: A tracking mechanism, not a pricing strategy.

prerequisites: a discount code system
steps: Create a code named only in content, not shared elsewhere.
Track redemptions by that code in the sales data.
Read redemptions monthly as one attribution signal, not the only one.

test.method: Track code redemptions in the monthly read.

title: Post a reorder reminder for consumable or replenishable products
hypothesis: If a 'time to reorder' post is timed to a consumable SKU's known use-up window and routed to the repeat-purchase segment, then reorders rise in that window compared to the prior cycle.
does_not_apply_when: durable, one-time-purchase products with no replenishment cycle

signal.check: A consumable SKU with a known use-up window has no reorder-reminder content tied to that window.

expected_effect.size: unknown; no library source, verify against brand data

risk.note: A timing and content addition only.

prerequisites: the SKU's known use-up window from order history
steps: Identify the SKU's average use-up window from order history.
Time a reorder-reminder post or Story to that window.
Route it to the repeat-purchase customer segment.
Track reorders in the window against the prior cycle.

test.method: Compare reorder rate in the reminder window to the prior cycle without the reminder.
test.read_point: One use-up cycle after the reminder starts

title: Check every number and claim against the brand record before publishing
hypothesis: If every number, study, result and comparison in a draft is checked against the brand record and PDP before publishing, then no invented claim reaches a customer.

signal.check: A draft contains a number, study result or comparison with no matching entry in the claims list.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a compliance rule, no lift given

risk.note: An unbacked claim published before the check can cause legal or trust damage.

prerequisites: the substantiated claims list
steps: List every number, study, result and comparison in the draft.
Check each against the brand record and the PDP.
Remove or replace any claim the brand record cannot back.
Get sign-off before publishing.

test.method: Audit a sample of published pieces monthly for unbacked claims.

title: Treat competitor and creator content as structure only, never copy the content
hypothesis: If competitor and creator content only ever supplies structure, pacing and mood, with no copied text, logos, products, faces or footage, then the brand avoids legal exposure while still learning from what works.

signal.check: A swipe entry, teardown or hook swap is being used with any of the source's actual text, footage, product or face carried over.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a compliance rule, no lift given

risk.note: Copied content can bring takedown, legal or platform action once published.

steps: Review any use of a competitor's ad, a creator's clip, or a swipe entry before publishing.
Confirm no text, logo, product, face or footage was copied.
Confirm any stitched third-party clip has confirmed usage rights.
Keep swipe files strictly for structure.

test.method: Run the compliance check comparing the piece to its source before publishing.
test.read_point: Before each publish that used a swipe or teardown source

title: Let the brand record's voice win over any source's tone advice
hypothesis: If informality, exaggeration, hot takes, first-person copy and negative framing are all treated as options to test inside the brand's voice rather than reasons to abandon it, then the account keeps a consistent voice while still testing tactics.

signal.check: A source-style suggestion (informal tone, exaggeration, hot takes, raw production) is being applied without checking it against the brand record's voice rules.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a governance rule, no lift given

risk.note: A style-governance check only.

prerequisites: the brand voice rules
steps: Check any borrowed tone tactic against the brand voice rules.
For regulated or luxury brands, default to the more formal register unless the brand record says otherwise.
Test the tactic only inside the voice's allowed range, never as a reason to leave it.

test.method: Audit a sample of posts monthly for voice-rule compliance.

title: Cap reading level below tenth grade on every piece of content
hypothesis: If every hook, script and caption stays below tenth grade, defaulting to the sources' stricter 5th to 8th grade target, then content stays accessible to the widest possible buyer audience.

signal.check: A piece scores at or above tenth grade on a readability check.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a house standard, not a measured lift

risk.note: An editing pass only.

prerequisites: a readability tool
steps: Run every piece through a readability checker before publishing.
Target 5th to 8th grade by default; never allow above 10th.
Simplify vocabulary and sentence structure until it passes.

test.method: Audit reading grade on a monthly sample of published content.

title: Route every controversial or comparative claim through legal review first
hypothesis: If every contrarian, versus, hot-take or counterfeit-style angle goes through a compliance and legal check before publishing, then the brand can use a true, defensible position without the defamation or platform-policy risk none of the sources actually assessed.

signal.check: A contrarian, versus or hot-take post is ready to publish with no legal or compliance review logged.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a compliance rule, no lift given

risk.note: An unreviewed accusation against a competitor can bring legal exposure once published.

prerequisites: access to legal review
steps: Flag any contrarian, versus, hot-take or counterfeit-style post before it is scheduled.
Confirm the position is true and the brand actually holds it.
Route it through legal review before publishing.
Confirm the owner will defend the position in the comments.

test.method: Track whether every flagged post has a logged legal or compliance sign-off before publishing.

title: Screen any post naming real people or news for defamation and endorsement risk
hypothesis: If any post that names a real person or a news story is screened for defamation and implied endorsement before publishing, then a topical or pop-culture hijack does not create legal exposure.

signal.check: A planned post names a real person, brand or news event with no defamation or endorsement screen logged.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a compliance rule, no lift given

risk.note: An unscreened post naming a real person can bring legal exposure once it is seen.

steps: Identify any real person, brand or news event named in the post.
Screen for defamation risk and implied endorsement.
Confirm permission is on file if a real person's likeness is used.
Log the screen before publishing.

test.method: Track whether every such post has a logged screen before publishing.

title: Never run a dangerous stunt for a hook or a challenge
hypothesis: If every hook and challenge idea is checked for danger before filming, then the brand keeps the attention benefit of a stretch or a drop test without the injury and liability risk of a real stunt.

signal.check: A hook or challenge idea involves a drop test, fire test or physical stunt with no safety check logged.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a safety rule, no lift given

risk.note: An actual injury from a filmed stunt cannot be undone.

steps: Identify any hook or challenge idea involving a physical stunt.
Check it against the safety screen in the compliance checklist.
Redesign the idea to remove the danger while keeping the stretch or surprise.

test.method: Confirm the safety screen was applied before filming any stunt-adjacent idea.
test.measure: pass rate on the safety check

title: Run a disclosure check before publishing any AI voice or synthetic footage
hypothesis: If any AI voiceover reuse or generated product image gets a disclosure and accuracy check before publishing, then the brand stays ahead of platform and regulatory disclosure rules and avoids misrepresenting the real product.

signal.check: A piece uses an AI voiceover, an AI spokesperson, or generated product imagery with no disclosure check logged.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a compliance rule, no lift given

risk.note: Undisclosed synthetic media can breach platform or regulatory rules once published.

prerequisites: current platform and regulatory disclosure rules, checked live
steps: Identify any AI voice, AI spokesperson or generated image in the piece.
Check current disclosure requirements for the platform and jurisdiction.
Add the required disclosure before publishing.
Use the real product photo instead of a generated image wherever accuracy matters.

test.method: Audit synthetic-media pieces for disclosure before publishing.

title: Run DM automation only inside current Meta policy with an approved partner
hypothesis: If comment-to-DM automation and follow-ups only run with a current approved partner and inside current messaging windows, then the funnel keeps working instead of being shut down or flagged for a policy breach.

signal.check: DM automation is live or planned with no current check of the approved-partner list or messaging window rules.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a compliance rule, no lift given

risk.note: A policy breach can pause or shut down the automation account.

prerequisites: current Meta messaging policy checked live
steps: Check the current approved DM automation partner list.
Confirm the chosen tool is on it.
Keep all follow-ups inside current messaging windows.
Recheck policy status at least quarterly and before any new campaign.

test.method: Confirm partner and policy status before every new DM campaign.
test.measure: pass or fail on the policy check
test.read_point: Before every new campaign and quarterly

title: Test raw or edgy content on a lower-stakes account for luxury or regulated brands
hypothesis: If a luxury or regulated brand tests raw, behind-the-scenes or edgy content on a lower-stakes account first, then it can learn whether the format works without risking the main brand's register.
does_not_apply_when: non-regulated, non-luxury brands

signal.check: A luxury, health or finance-adjacent brand is about to run raw or edgy content on its main account.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a risk-management rule, no lift given

risk.note: Raw content on the wrong account for a regulated brand can damage trust before it is caught.

prerequisites: a secondary, lower-stakes account or content line
steps: Flag the brand's regulated or luxury status in the account foundations document.
Route raw or edgy format tests to a secondary account instead of the main one.
Review results before ever moving a format to the main account.
Skip the format entirely if no safe test account exists.

test.method: Compare engagement on the secondary-account test to the main account's normal register.

title: Turn shipping and returns policy clarity into pre-purchase trust content
hypothesis: If a short post or Story explains free returns, delivery time or a guarantee, matched exactly to the live policy page, then hesitant first-time buyers get the reassurance that stalls them at checkout.

signal.check: Checkout hesitation is a known drop-off point, or comments repeatedly ask about delivery and returns.

expected_effect.size: unknown; no library source, verify against brand data

risk.note: The stated policy must exactly match the live policy page to avoid a false claim.

prerequisites: the current, live shipping and returns policy
steps: Pull the exact current shipping and returns policy from the live policy page.
Build a short post or Story explaining the policy in plain language, matched exactly to what is live.
Track checkout completion and delivery-related comments after the post.

test.method: Compare checkout completion rate and delivery questions before and after the post.

title: Run the start-generate-test-measure-scale loop on one strong idea
hypothesis: If one strong idea is turned into 10 or more hook, cut and caption variations and 3 to 5 are published in a short window, then the team gets a fast read on which version to scale instead of guessing from a single post.

signal.check: A strong idea exists but only 1 version has ever been made and published, with no variation test run.

expected_effect.size: unknown; process claim, no lift given; treat 1 round as a signal and 3 rounds as a pattern (unsourced house default)

risk.note: A test-round design only; no downside beyond production time.

prerequisites: 1 strong core idea
the ability to publish several variations in a short window
steps: Start with 1 core idea.
Generate 10 or more variations: hook types and framings, cuts, per-platform captions, benefit emphasis.
Publish the chosen 3 to 5 within a short window, ideally the same time of day.
Measure completion, saves, comments, replays and CTR, not raw views.
Scale the winner across platforms and formats.
Log losers by hook type for the next round.
Treat 1 round as a signal only; treat 3 rounds as a pattern before drawing a firm conclusion.

test.method: Compare the pre-set metrics across the 3 to 5 variations after the test window.
test.read_point: After the test window closes, confirmed after 3 rounds

title: Pick 1 hero SKU per post instead of a generic 'our products' post
hypothesis: If a wide-catalogue store features exactly 1 hero SKU per post instead of a generic 'our products' post, then the content gives a clear next step to one product instead of diffusing attention across many.
does_not_apply_when: hero-SKU stores, which already default to featuring their one product

signal.check: A post shows multiple products with no single featured SKU, or the caption says 'our products' with no specific item named.

expected_effect.size: unknown; general practice, verify against brand data

risk.note: A content-planning rule only.

prerequisites: the SKU rotation plan
steps: Check the calendar for any post with no single featured SKU.
Pick 1 hero SKU per post from the rotation plan.
Confirm the post's link and CTA point to that same SKU's PDP.
Avoid generic multi-product framing except for true collection or bundle posts.

test.method: Compare cvr_pdp_to_cart on single-SKU posts vs multi-product posts.

title: Log every post's real useful point and its entertaining wrapper separately
hypothesis: If every post is checked for a real, useful point delivered inside an entertaining wrapper (a format, a scenario, a story, speed, a prop), and both are logged, then the monthly read can show the brand's own balance instead of guessing whether education or entertainment drives results.

signal.check: A post is either pure entertainment with no real product point, or pure education with no entertaining delivery, and this split has never been logged.

expected_effect.size: unknown; the sides mostly describe the same content in different words, no shared lift number

risk.note: A tagging and content-review rule only.

steps: Check each post for a real, useful point about the product.
Check each post for an entertaining delivery: a format, scenario, story, speed or prop.
Reject or rework posts that are only one of the two.
Log which pillar and which wrapper each post used.
Read the balance monthly across the account.

test.method: Track the split of education-only, entertainment-only and both-present posts each month.

title: Put proof in positioning and personality in stories; let credibility lead for considered purchases
hypothesis: If proof lives in the positioning statement and every claim, while personality lives in the stories and delivery, then the account gets both trust and relatability, with credibility given more weight for considered or regulated purchases.

signal.check: The account leans entirely on personality with no verifiable proof anywhere, or entirely on credentials with no relatable delivery.

expected_effect.size: unknown; a merged rule between 2 sources with different emphasis, no shared lift number

risk.note: A positioning and content-balance decision only.

prerequisites: the positioning statement and story set already built
steps: Confirm the positioning statement carries a real, verifiable proof point.
Confirm claims across content trace back to that proof point.
Deliver personality and relatability through stories, not through unverifiable claims.
For a considered or regulated purchase, weight credibility higher than personality in the content mix.

test.method: Track trust-related engagement (saves, DM questions about credibility) across content emphasizing proof vs personality.

title: Warm up with 10 to 15 minutes of copywork before high-stakes copy
hypothesis: If a writer hand-copies or types 10 to 15 minutes of admired writing in the target tone before drafting a high-stakes piece, then the draft starts closer to the intended voice and rhythm, because the warm-up primes plain, persuasive sentence patterns before the writer's own words start.
does_not_apply_when: short captions, which can skip this step

signal.check: A writer starts a landing page, founder letter or key campaign script cold, with no warm-up exercise.

expected_effect.size: unknown; presenter's personal practice, no lift given

risk.note: A short pre-writing exercise only; costs a few minutes.

prerequisites: a swipe file of admired writing in the target tone
steps: Pick a swipe-file piece that matches the tone the new piece needs.
Hand-copy or type that piece word for word for 10 to 15 minutes without improving it.
Move straight into drafting the real piece while the rhythm is fresh.
Skip this step for short captions; keep it for landing pages, founder letters and key campaign scripts.

test.method: Compare reviewer notes and edit time on copywork-warmed pieces against cold-started pieces.
test.read_point: Reviewer pass after the next 5 high-stakes pieces
